findings.source_passage: The last swimmers have come in from the beach now and are dressing upstairs; the cars from New York are parked five deep in the drive
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'By seven o'clock the orchestra has arrived'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'last swimmers... dressing upstairs' clause is part of the present-tense party set-piece's signature rhythm; cutting it shortens the famous cadence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full clause before 'the cars from New York are parked five deep in the drive.'

findings.source_passage: moving her hands like Frisco, dances out alone on the canvas platform
findings.source_locator: paragraph 'Suddenly one of these gypsies, in trembling opal'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'moving her hands like Frisco' simile is a period-specific signature gesture (referencing Frisco the dancer); its removal flattens Fitzgerald's pop-cultural texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'and, moving her hands like Frisco,' before 'dances out alone.'

findings.source_passage: "I don't think it's so much that," argued Lucille sceptically; "It's more that he was a German spy during the war." ... "You look at him sometimes when he thinks nobody's looking at him. I'll bet he killed a man."
findings.why_it_matters: The plan explicitly says 'keep one rumor, cut the others to a gesture' — the draft cuts ALL rumor exchange after the killed-a-man line, losing the German-spy rumor and the 'I'll bet he killed a man' eye-narrowing shiver entirely. The cumulative effect of layered rumor is the scene's signature.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least a brief gesture toward the German-spy rumor and the 'narrowed her eyes and shivered' beat to retain the mythologizing texture.

findings.source_passage: stocked with gins and liquors and with cordials so long forgotten
findings.why_it_matters: The 'gins and liquors and' triplet is part of Fitzgerald's catalogue rhythm; truncating to just 'cordials' loses a beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'gins and liquors and with cordials so long forgotten.'

findings.source_passage: But what do you want? What do you expect?
findings.source_locator: Owl Eyes library scene, after 'didn't cut the pages'
findings.why_it_matters: These two clipped rhetorical questions are part of Owl Eyes' signature cadence in the library scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Append 'But what do you want? What do you expect?' after 'didn't cut the pages.'

summary: Major signatures (blue gardens, oranges-and-lemons, seven-o'clock orchestra, yellow cocktail music, Gatsby's smile, roughneck, Owl Eyes, twilight digression, 'few honest people') are preserved largely verbatim; medium losses are confined to small phrasing trims and the over-aggressive cut of the rumor exchange.
